evidence.claim: The loop joins two of New Hampshire’s four original towns with two communities later divided from them.
evidence.quote: two of New Hampshire’s four original towns -- Exeter (1638) and Hampton (1639) - and two of the smaller towns that were later divided from them— Hampton Falls and Kensington

evidence.claim: Exeter became a center of revolutionary government after royal governor John Wentworth barred the Provincial Congress from Portsmouth in 1774.
evidence.quote: In 1774, the rebellious Provincial Congress began to meet in the Exeter Town House after colonial governor John Wentworth banned it from the colonial capitol at Portsmouth.

evidence.claim: The following year, the Congress brought seized provincial records to Exeter, which served as the capital for 14 years.
evidence.quote: In July 1775, the Provincial Congress had the provincial records seized from royal officials in Portsmouth and brought to Exeter, as well, so Exeter became New Hampshire's capital, an honor it held for 14 years.
